* I'rab:
(أم) in the sense of بل; (الذي) a relative in the position of nominative as a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (جند); (من دون) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of ينصركم; (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (في غرور) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الكافرون).
The clause «من هذا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو جند ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «ينصركم ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of جند.
The clause «إن الكافرون إلّا في غرور» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Benefits:
- The negative إن:
It enters upon the nominal clause, as in His words: (إِنِ الْكافِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ) (وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها), and it enters upon the verbal clause, as in His words: «إِنْ أَرَدْنا إِلَّا الْحُسْنى» «إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا إِناثاً». Some said: the negative (إن) only comes with (إلا) after it. This view is rejected, by the evidence of His words: (إِنْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ بِهذا) (قُلْ إِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ). When it enters upon the nominal clause it does not govern according to Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, while al-Kisāʾī and al-Mubarrad permitted it to govern as ليس governs. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبادٌ أَمْثالُكُمْ), and it was heard from the people of al-ʿĀliya: «إن أحد خيرا من أحد إلا بالعافية» ("No one is better than anyone except by well-being"). But most grammarians consider it a negative particle that is left ungoverning (muhmala), having no grammatical effect. [Translator's note: the reading attributed to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr is printed in the source as «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ ... عِبادٌ أَمْثالُكُمْ»; the reading usually cited for him, which illustrates إن governing like ليس, is «إِنِ الَّذِينَ ... عِبَاداً أَمْثَالَكُمْ». Translated as printed.]
21-

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(أم من هذا الذي): its i'rab has already been given [Note: In the previous verse (20).]; (أمسك) a past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil (agent) being a pronoun referring to Allah; (بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (في عتوّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of لجّوا ...
The clause «من هذا الذي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يرزقكم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أمسك رزقه ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes.
The clause «لجّوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
22-

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation seeking acknowledgement (taqrīr); (الفاء) resumptive; (من) a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is (أهدى); (على وجهه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مكبّا); (أم) a conjunction counterbalancing the hamza; (من) a relative in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first relative; (على صراط) attached to (يمشي) ...
The clause «من يمشي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يمشي» (the first) has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «يمشي» (the second) has no grammatical position: ṣila of the (second) relative (من).

* Morphology:
(مكبّا): active participle of the quadriliteral أكبّ. Its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn; its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His words «أَفَمَنْ يَمْشِي مُكِبًّا عَلى وَجْهِهِ أَهْدى أَمَّنْ يَمْشِي سَوِيًّا عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ».
A similitude struck for the polytheist and the monotheist, to clarify their states and establish the nature of their ways: the polytheist is blind, not finding his way to the road, walking aimlessly, so he keeps stumbling and falling on his face; and the monotheist has sound sight, walking on a clear, straight road, safe from stumbling and falling on his face.
23-

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction in the three places; (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of السمع, الأبصار and الأفئدة [Note: By making جعل carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of خلق ... and it is attached to a second object if it is in its usual sense.]; (قليلا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, for it is its description, governed by تشكرون, accusative; (ما) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the paucity.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو الذي ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنشأكم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila clause.
The clause «تشكرون» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in (لكم).].
24-

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(في الأرض) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ذرأكم); (الواو) conjunction; (إليه) attached to (تحشرون).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو الذي ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ذرأكم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «إليه تحشرون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila clause.
25-

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (متى) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هذا); (كنتم) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ...
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «متى هذا الوعد ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «كنتم صادقين ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying.
26-

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) the restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa) in both places; (عند) an accusative adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (العلم); (الواو) conjunction ...
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «العلم عند الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنا نذير ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object of speech.
27-

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لمّا) an adverb in the sense of "when", containing the meaning of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis سيئت, and (الهاء) in (رأوه) refers to the punishment; (زلفة) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun in (رأوه), accusative; (به) attached to (تدّعون) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. its warning ...
The clause «رأوه ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «سيئت وجوه ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause سيئت. The clause «هذا الذي ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: Because it is originally the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of the active verb ... and some make it an explanation of the implied nāʾib fāʿil, i.e. "the saying was said".].
The clause «كنتم به تدّعون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «تدّعون» is in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(زلفة): a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the quadriliteral أزلف; this noun is in the sense of the active participle, i.e. مزلف, that is, near. Its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn.
(سيئت): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution: the yāʾ was originally a wāw preceded by a kasra. The vowel of the sīn was originally [Translator's note: the source leaves the original vowel unnamed; a ḍamma is evidently meant], and it was given kasra to suit the passive voice; then the wāw was changed into yāʾ to escape the heaviness resulting from moving from ḍamma to kasra, to suit the passive voice ...
(قيل): it contains iʿlāl like سيئت ...
28-

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(أرأيتم), i.e. "tell me"; the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, its implied form being "your affair" or "your state"; (أهلكني) a past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الواو) conjunction; (من) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object pronoun in (أهلكني); (أو) a conjunction ... (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (من) an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (من عذاب) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يجير) ...
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أرأيتم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أهلكني الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb of seeing.
The clause «رحمنا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause أهلكني الله.
The clause «من يجير ...» has no grammatical position: a causal explanation of the implied apodosis, i.e.: whether I die or live, there is no benefit for you in that, because there is no protector for you from the punishment of Allah ...
The clause «يجير ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من).
29-

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(به) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آمنّا); (الواو) conjunction; (عليه) attached to (توكّلنا); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (السين) a particle of futurity; (من) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: Or an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the preposition and its genitive noun (في ضلال ...), with (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), the nominal clause filling the place of the two objects of ستعلمون, which is suspended by the interrogative.]; (في ضلال) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, emphasising the preceding resumption [Note: In the previous verse (28).].
The clause «هو الرحمن ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «آمنّا به» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying. The clause «توكّلنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause آمنّا به.
The clause «ستعلمون ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if the punishment comes to you, you will know.
The clause «هو في ضلال ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
30-

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
The i'rab of a parallel of this verse has already been given «1»; (بماء) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتيكم).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, emphasising the preceding resumption «2».
The clause «رأيتم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أصبح ماؤكم غورا ...» is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb رأيتم.
The clause «من يأتيكم ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يأتيكم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (من).

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ}: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَلَقَ». His saying «أيُّكم أحسنُ»: something like it has preceded at the beginning of Hūd. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: in what way is His saying {أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلاً} connected with the verb of testing? I say: in that it includes the meaning of knowing, so it is as if it were said: so that He may make known [of] you which of you is best in deed. And if you say: 'I knew him — is Zayd better in deed, or is he?', this clause stands in the place of the second of its two objects, just as you say: 'I knew him to be better in deed.' If you say: do you call this taʿlīq (suspension)? I say: no; taʿlīq is only when what comes after it stands in place of both objects together, as in your saying: 'I knew which of the two is ʿAmr', and 'I knew: is Zayd departing?'. Do you not see that, once one of the two objects has come first, there is no difference between what follows it being headed by an interrogative particle and its not being headed by one? Had it been taʿlīq, the two situations would have differed, just as they differ in your saying: 'I knew: is Zayd departing?' and 'I knew Zayd to be departing.'"
I say: what he refused to call taʿlīq, others have called by that name, and they make that clause in the position of the noun to which that verb passes over. So they say regarding «عَرَفْت أيُّهم منطلقٌ» ("I knew which of them is departing"): the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative because it stands in place of the object of «عَرَفْتُ»; and regarding «نَظَرْتُ أيُّهم منطلقٌ» ("I looked into which of them is departing"): the clause is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (isqāṭ al-khāfiḍ), because «نظر» passes over [to its object] by means of it.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {الذي خَلَقَ}: it may be a follower of «العزيز الغفور» — as a naʿt (adjective), a bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal (substitute) — or it may be cut off from it, as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject), or the object of an implied (muqaddar) verb.
His saying: {طِبَاقاً}: an adjective of «سبعَ». There are three views on it. The first: that it is the plural of طَبَق, like جَبَل and جِبال. The second: that it is the plural of طَبَقة, like رَقَبة and رِقاب. The third: that it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of طابَقَ; one says طابقَ مُطابقة وطِباقاً. Then: either the maṣdar itself is made [the description] for intensiveness; or it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. ذاتَ طباق ("possessing layers"); or it is accusative as an absolute object by an implied verb, i.e. طُوْبِقَتْ طباقاً ("they were layered in layering"), from their saying طابَقَ النعلَ, i.e. he made it one layer upon another.
His saying: {مِن تَفَاوُتٍ}: it is the object of «تَرَى», and «مِنْ» is redundant (mazīda) in it. The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «تَفَوُّتٍ» with the wāw doubled and no alif; the rest read it with it undoubled after an alif. They are two dialectal forms with one meaning, like التعهُّد and التعاهد, and التظهُّر and التظاهُر. Abū Zayd related: "تفاوَتَ الشيءُ تفاوُتاً with the wāw vowelled with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra; the analogical form is the ḍamma, as in التقابُل, while the fatḥa and the kasra are anomalous." And التفاوُت is the absence of proportion, because some parts pass beyond (yafūtu) others. This negated clause is an adjective that accompanies His saying «طباقاً»; its original form is: "you do not see in them", and in place of the pronoun He put His saying {خَلْقِ الرحمن}, in exaltation of their creation and as a pointer to the cause of their soundness, which is that it is the creation of the All-Merciful — al-Zamakhsharī said this. What this apparently means is that it is an adjective of «طباقاً» in which the overt noun stands in place of the pronoun; but this we know only in the predicate of a mubtadaʾ and in the ṣila (relative clause), and even there with disagreement and detail.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What is apparent is that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf)." It is not apparent, because it makes the parts of the discourse come loose from one another.
And «خَلْق» is a maṣdar annexed to its agent, with the object omitted, i.e. in the All-Merciful's creation of the heavens, or of every created thing — and this is preferable, so that it is general, even if the context points to the first.
His saying: {فارجع}: it is consequent upon His saying «ما تَرَى». And «كرَّتَيْن» is accusative as a maṣdar, like «مرَّتَيْن» ("twice"). It is a dual whose literal meaning is not intended; rather multiplicity is intended, as shown by His saying {يَنْقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ البَصَرُ خَاسِئاً وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ}, i.e. repelled while it is fatigued; these two qualities do not come about from two looks, nor three. The meaning is only: repeated times. This is like their saying لَبَّيْك وسَعْديك وحنانَيْك ودَواليك وهذاذَيْك: by this dual they do not mean the pairing of a single one; they mean only multiplicity, i.e. a response to you after another response — otherwise the purpose would be self-contradictory. The dual conveys multiplicity through a contextual indicator (qarīna), just as its origin conveys it, namely conjunction, through a contextual indicator, as in his saying:
4282 - لو عُدَّ قبرٌ كنتَ أكرَمَهم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Were a grave [and a grave] counted, you would be the noblest of them …)
i.e. many «قبول» [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently «قبور», "graves", is meant], so that the praise is complete. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«كَرَّتَيْن» means «مَرَّتَيِن» (twice), and its accusative is as a maṣdar." It was said: the first [look] is so that its beauty and evenness may be seen, and the second so that its stars may be observed in their course and their end. This is an outward reading that conveys only the dual.
His saying: {هَلْ ترى مِن فُطُورٍ}: this clause may be the object of suspension (taʿlīq) of an omitted verb indicated by «فارْجِعِ البصر», i.e. then return your sight and look: do you see …; or «فارجعِ البصر» may include the meaning of "look", since it has its meaning, so that it is the suspended verb. Abū ʿAmr assimilated the lām of «هل» into the tāʾ here and in al-Ḥāqqa, while the rest pronounced it clearly, which is the well-known usage in the language.
And الفُطور means cracks and fissures. He said:
4283 - شَقَقْتُ القلب ثم ذَرَرْتُ فيه ... هواكِ فَلِيْطَ فالتأَمَ الفُطورُ
(I split the heart, then sprinkled your love into it, and it adhered, and the cracks closed up.)

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {يَنْقَلِبْ}: the majority read it in the jussive as the answer to the imperative; al-Kisāʾī, in one transmission, read it in the nominative. There are two views on this. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) that is anticipated (muqaddara). The second: that it is on the omission of the fāʾ, i.e. فينقلِبْ. And «خاسِئاً» is a ḥāl, and His saying «وهو حسيرٌ» is a ḥāl either of the owner of the first [ḥāl], or of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the ḥāl before it, so that they are interlocking (mutadākhila). The roots of «خاسئاً» and «حسيراً» have preceded in al-Muʾminūn and al-Anbiyāʾ.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {الدنيا}: [meaning] the one nearest to you (minkum), because it is a fuʿlā form, the feminine of the elative afʿal. [Translator's note: the text reads «[يعني] منكم», evidently with a word such as «القربى» ("the nearest") dropped before «منكم».] And «جَعَلْناها»: two views are permissible regarding the pronoun. The first: that it refers back to «مَصابيحَ», which is the apparent one. It was said: the manner of the pelting is that fire is taken from the light of the star and the devil is pelted with it, while the star stays in its place and is not itself pelted with. The second: that the pronoun refers back to the sky, the meaning being "from it", because the sky itself is not for pelting — the Shaykh said this. There is a point to consider in it, since the pronoun's referring back to the sky is not apparent. And الرُّجوم is the plural of رَجْم, which is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), applied to what is pelted with, like «ضَرْبِ الأميرِ» ("the prince's coinage"). It may remain as a maṣdar, with a muḍāf implied, i.e. ذاتُ رُجوم ("possessing peltings"), the maṣdar being pluralised in view of its kinds. On the first [view], His saying «للشياطين» is attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «رُجوماً»; on the second, it has no attachment, because the lām is redundant on the direct object — and then there is in it evidence for the governing of a maṣdar that has tanwīn and is in the plural. It may also be an adjective of it, as in the first [view], so that it is attached to an omitted element. It was said: الرُّجوم here means conjectures, and the devils are the devils of mankind, as he said:
4283 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
وما هو عنها بالحديثِ المُرَجَّمِ
(… and it is not, concerning it, a conjectured report.) [Translator's note: the verse number 4283 repeats the number of the previous verse; so in the text.]

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ}: it is a fronted khabar (predicate) in the reading of the majority, and «عذابُ جهنَم» is its mubtadaʾ (subject). In the reading of al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Aʿraj, with it in the accusative, it is attached to «أَعْتَدْنا», conjoined to «لهم», and «عذابَ جهنمَ» is conjoined to «عذابَ السعير»: so an accusative is conjoined to an accusative and a genitive to a genitive, and the preposition is repeated because what is conjoined to is a pronoun. The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "and evil is the destination — their destination", or "the punishment of Hell", or "the punishment of the Blaze".

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {لَهَا}: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «شهيقاً», because it was originally its adjective. It may also be on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. they heard from its people. And «وهي تفور» is a circumstantial clause.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {تَمَيَّزُ}: this is the reading of the majority, with a single, undoubled tāʾ. The original is تتميَّزُ with two tāʾs. Ṭalḥa read it so, and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr [read it] with it doubled, assimilating one of the two tāʾs into the other — and it is a good reading, since there is no meeting of two quiescent letters, unlike his reading {إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ} [al-Nūr: 15] and {نَاراً تلظى} [al-Layl: 14] and the like. Abū ʿAmr assimilates the dāl into the tāʾ, according to his principle with letters close in articulation. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «تمايَزُ», the original being تتمايَزُ with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «تَمِيْزُ», from ماز. All of this is a metaphor from their saying: "So-and-so تميَّز من الغيظ", i.e. parts of him split from others out of rage; so «مِنْ» is causal, i.e. because of rage. Like it is [the saying of the rajaz poet] describing a dog whose running became intense:
4285 - يكادُ أَنْ يخرجَ مِنْ إهابِهْ
(It almost comes out of its skin.)
His saying: {كُلَّمَا أُلْقِيَ}: the discussion of «كلما» has preceded. This clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun referring to Jahannam.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {بلى قَدْ جَآءَنَا نَذِيرٌ}: in it is evidence for the permissibility of combining the answer particle with the very clause answered by it, since had they said "بلى" the meaning would have been understood; but they made it explicit out of regret and as an increase in their grief at their negligence in accepting the word of the warner, and so as to conjoin to it their saying «فكذَّبْنا» to the end.
His saying: {إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلاَّ فِي ضَلاَلٍ}: its apparent sense is that it is part of what the unbelievers said to the warner. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be the speech of the messengers to the unbelievers, which the unbelievers relate to the keepers [of Hell], i.e. they said this to us and we did not accept it.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {بِذَنبِهِمْ}: He made it singular because it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and diversity of kinds was not intended — unlike «بذنوبهم» in [other] places.
His saying: {فَسُحْقاً}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. Allah imposed on them remoteness. The second: that it is accusative as a maṣdar, its implied form being "Allah made them remote, a remoteness", the maṣdar standing in for its governor in imprecation, as in جَدْعاً له وعَقْراً ("mutilation to him and wounding"); so its governor may not be made overt. The grammarians disagreed: is it the maṣdar of a three-letter verb, or of a four-letter verb that came with its augments dropped? Al-Fārisī and al-Zajjāj held that it is the maṣdar of أسْحَقَه اللَّهُ, i.e. He removed him far. Al-Fārisī said: "The analogical form would have been إسْحاقاً, but the maṣdar came with omission, as in his saying:
4286 - فإن أَهْلِكْ فذلك كان قَدْري ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If I perish, that was my decree …)
i.e. تقديري ("my decreeing")." What is apparent is that this is not needed, because سَحَقه اللَّهُ has been heard as a three-letter verb. There is about it the poet's saying:
4287 - يجولُ بأطرافِ البلادِ مُغَرِّباً ... وتَسْحَقُه ريحُ الصَّبا كلَّ مَسْحَقِ
(He roams the far ends of the lands, heading west, while the east wind drives him off to every far place.)
What appears is that al-Zajjāj and al-Fārisī said that only regarding those Arabs who say أَسْحقه الله سُحْقاً.
The majority read it with a ḍamma and a sukūn; al-Kisāʾī, among others, read it with two ḍammas. They are two dialectal forms, and it is better that the heavy form be the origin of the light one. And [His saying] «لأصحاب» is explicative (bayān), like {هَيْتَ لَكَ} [Yūsuf: 23] and سَقْياً لك ("rain to you"). Makkī said: "The nominative is permissible in speech, as a mubtadaʾ (subject)", i.e. had it been said «فَسُحْقٌ» it would have been permissible — not as a recitation, but from the standpoint of grammatical craft. However, Ibn ʿAṭiyya said something that weakens it, for he said: "«فسُحْقاً» is accusative by way of imprecation against them. That was permissible in it although it is from Allah the Exalted, inasmuch as this saying is established concerning them first, while its realisation has not occurred and will not occur except in the Hereafter; so for that reason it is as if in the domain of the expected, which is prayed for, as you say: 'Remoteness to Zayd, and distance to him'. The accusative in all this is by an implied (muḍmar) verb. As for what has occurred and become established, the proper form in it is the nominative, as He the Exalted said: {وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ} [al-Muṭaffifīn: 1], {سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم} [al-Raʿd: 24], and other examples." End of quote. So he weakened the nominative, as you see, because it has not occurred but is expected in the Hereafter.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ}: the best is that the khabar (predicate) be «لهم» and «مغفرةٌ» be a fāʿil (agent) by it, because the single-word predicate is the basic one, and the preposition phrase belongs to the category of single words or is closer to them.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {مَنْ خَلَقَ}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is the fāʿil (agent) of «يَعْلَمُ», with the object omitted, its implied form being: "Does not the Creator know His creation?" This is the view of the majority of people, and al-Zamakhsharī began with it. The second: that the agent is a latent pronoun referring to the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, and «مَنْ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. does Allah not know whom He created? The Shaykh said: "What is apparent is that «مَنْ» is an object, the meaning being: is His knowledge of those He created negated, when He is the One whose knowledge is subtle and fine?" Then he said: "Some grammarians allowed «مَنْ» to be an agent with the object omitted, as if He said: does not the Creator know your secret and your open [speech]? It is a question whose meaning is denial." I say: this view, which he made the apparent one, people attribute to the people of deviation (al-zayʿ) [Translator's note: so in the text; «الزيغ» as below] and innovation, who reject the generality of [Allah's] creating for Allah the Exalted.
Makkī elaborated on this at length, rejected whoever holds it, and ascribed it to what I have mentioned, saying: "One of the people of deviation said: «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative, a noun for those who conceal and those who speak openly, so as to take the discourse out of its generality and to deny Allah the Exalted the generality of creating. Had it been as he claimed, He would have said: 'Does He not know what He created?', because what was mentioned before is only what breasts conceal, so it stands in the place of «ما». And had «ما» come in the place of «مَنْ», there would also have been in it a statement of generality: that Allah is the Creator of everything of the creatures' words, whether they concealed them or made them public, whether good or evil. This is strengthened by {إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصدور} — He did not say: 'Knowing of those who conceal and those who speak openly' — with «ما» in the position of the accusative. The verse is taken out of this generality only if you make «مَنْ» in the position of the accusative as a noun for the people addressed before this verse; and His saying «بذات الصدورِ» prevents that." End of quote. I do not know how what Makkī said follows necessarily from the i'rab he mentioned and the meaning he put forward. This view — I mean the second i'rab — was held by a number of the meticulous scholars, and they paid no heed to what he mentioned, since the verse does not convey it.
Al-Zamakhsharī said, after some words he mentioned: "Then He denied that the One who created things should not encompass in knowledge what is concealed, what is kept secret and what is spoken openly, His state being that He is the Subtle, the All-Aware, whose knowledge reaches what is outward and what is hidden. And «مَنْ خَلَقَ» may be accusative, meaning: does He not know what He has created, this being His state?" Then he said: "If you say: you implied an object in «ألا يَعْلَمُ», in the sense: does not the one who created know that which was mentioned, of what is concealed in the heart and expressed by the tongue? Why did you not make it like their saying 'He gives and withholds', and why was the meaning not: is not the one who is a creator knowing, since creating is not valid except with knowledge? I say: the ḥāl (circumstantial) — His saying {وَهُوَ اللطيف الخبير} — refuses that, because were you to say: 'Is not the one who is a creator knowing, while He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?', the meaning would not be sound; for «ألا يَعْلَمُ» depends on the ḥāl, and a thing is not timed by itself. So one does not say: 'Does He not know, while He is knowing?', but rather: 'Does He not know such-and-such, while He is knowing of everything?'"

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {ذَلُولاً}: a second object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial). And ذَلول is a faʿūl form for intensiveness from ذَلَّ يَذِلُّ فهو ذالٌّ, as in the saying: "a docile (ذَلولٌ) mount, evidently docile (الذِّلّ, with kasra)", and "a humble (ذَلُولٌ) man, evidently humble (الذُّلّ, with ḍamma)". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "ذلول is a faʿūl form in the sense of mafʿūl, i.e. مَذْلولة, so it is like رَكوب and حَلوب." The Shaykh said: "It is not in the sense of mafʿūl, because its verb is intransitive (qāṣir); it is made transitive only by the hamza, as in His saying {وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَآءُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 26], or by doubling, as in His saying {وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا لَهُمْ} [Yā Sīn: 72]. His saying 'i.e. مَذْلولة' appears to be a mistake." End of quote — he means: inasmuch as he used the passive participle fully from an intransitive verb. This is a verbal quibble.
His saying: {مَنَاكِبِهَا}: a very fine metaphor. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a figure for the excess of subjugation and its exceeding the limit, because the two shoulders and where they meet at the withers are the most delicate part of a camel and the least suited to a rider treading on it with his foot and leaning on it. So when He made it so docile that one walks on its shoulders, He left nothing [undone]."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {أَأَمِنتُمْ}: the disagreement of the readers over two hamzas with fatḥa, as in {أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 6] — pronouncing them fully or lightening them, and inserting an alif between them or not — has preceded in al-Baqara; and also that Qunbul here reads by changing the first hamza into a wāw in continuous recitation, saying: {وَإِلَيْهِ النشور} {وَأَمِنْتُمْ}, and he is according to his principle [Translator's note: the text has «صلِه», evidently for «أصله»] of easing the second between-between (bayna bayna) and not having an alif between them. But when he begins [with the word], he pronounces the first fully and eases the second between-between as stated before, and does not change the first into a wāw, because its cause has disappeared — namely, what precedes it having a ḍamma while it has a fatḥa, as in مُوَجَّل and يُواخِذُكم. This has passed in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf at His saying {قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ آمَنتُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 123]; I have repeated it only as explanation and reminder.
His saying: {مَّن فِي السمآء}: the object of «أَمِنْتُم». In the discourse there is the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. have you felt secure from the Creator of whoever is in the heavens? It was also said: «في» is in the sense of «على», i.e. upon the heaven. The one who held these two views needed that only because he believed that «مَنْ» applies to the Creator, exalted is He — which is the apparent sense — while it is established by decisive proof that He is not confined in space, lest anthropomorphism (tajsīm) follow. There is no need for that, for what is meant by «مَنْ» here is the angels, the inhabitants of heaven, who are the ones charged with mercy and vengeance. It was also said: they were addressed thus according to their own belief, for those people were anthropomorphists who likened [Allah to creation]. What preceded is better.
His saying: {أَن يَخْسِفَ} and «أَنْ يرسلَ»: there are two views on them. The first: that they are both badal (substitute) of «مَنْ في السماء», a badal of inclusion (ishtimāl), i.e. have you felt secure from His causing to sink and His sending — Abū al-Baqāʾ said so. The second: that it is on the omission of «مِنْ», i.e. have you felt secure from the sinking and the sending. The first is more apparent. It has preceded that «نذير» and «نكير» are maṣdars in the sense of إنذار (warning) and إنكار (disapproval). Warsh kept the yāʾ of «نَذيري» in pause and dropped it in continuation; the rest dropped it in both cases.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {صَافَّاتٍ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الطير», or a ḥāl of the pronoun in «فوقَهم» if we make that a ḥāl, so that they are interlocking (mutadākhila). And «فوقَهم» is an adverb (ẓarf) for «صافَّات» on the first [view], or for «يَرَوْا».
His saying: {وَيَقْبِضْنَ}: He conjoined the verb to the noun because it has its meaning, i.e. وقابضاتٍ ("and folding"); so the verb here is interpreted as the noun — the reverse of His saying {إِنَّ المصدقين والمصدقات وَأَقْرَضُواْ} [al-Ḥadīd: 18], for there the noun is interpreted as the verb. The objection to that has preceded. As for Abū al-Baqāʾ's saying: "It is conjoined to the active participle, construed according to the meaning, i.e. they spread and they fold, i.e. spreading and folding" — there is no need to imply "they spread and they fold", because the slot is for the noun, so we do not interpret it as a verb. The Shaykh said: "He conjoined the verb to the noun since it is in its meaning; similar is His saying the Exalted {فالمغيرات صُبْحاً فَأَثَرْنَ} [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 3-4]: He conjoined the verb to the noun since the meaning is 'those who raided and raised [dust]'. Such conjunction is eloquent, and so is its reverse — except according to al-Suhaylī, for whom it is ugly — as in his saying:
4288 - بات يُغَشِّيها بعَضْبٍ باترٍ ... يَقْصِدُ في أسْوُقِها وجائِرُ
(He spent the night covering them with a cutting sword, aiming at their shanks and going astray.)
i.e. aiming at their shanks and going astray." End of quote. That is like it in conjoining a verb to a noun, except that the noun in it is interpreted as a verb, the reverse of this verse. The object of «يَقْبِضْنَ» is omitted, i.e. and they fold their wings — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this; he did not imply an object for «صافَّاتٍ», as if he claimed that the lining up is in themselves, i.e. lined up. What is apparent is that the meaning is: spreading their wings and folding them; so the spreading and the folding are of their wings by them.
Likewise al-Zamakhsharī said: "«صافَّاتٍ»: stretching out their wings." Then he said: "If you say: why did He say «ويقبضْنَ» and not say وقابضاتٍ? I say: because flying is the spreading of the wings, since flying in the air is like swimming in water, and the basic thing in swimming is extending the limbs and stretching them out; as for folding, it is something occurring upon the stretching, to gain help from it in moving. So what is occurring and not basic was brought in the form of a verb, in the sense that they are spreading, and folding occurs from them time after time, as it does from a swimmer."
His saying: {مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ}: the clause may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa), or a ḥāl of the pronoun in «يَقْبِضْنَ» — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this; the first is the apparent one. Al-Zuhrī read it with the sīn doubled.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {أَمَّن}: the majority read it with the mīm doubled, by assimilating the mīm of «أم» into the mīm of «مَنْ»; and «أم» is in the sense of «بل», because after it is an interrogative noun, which is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the demonstrative. Ṭalḥa read it with the first undoubled and the second doubled. Abū al-Faḍl said: "Its meaning is: is this the one who is an army for you, or the one who provides for you?" And «يَنْصُرُكم» is an adjective of «جند».

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {إِنْ أَمْسَكَ}: a conditional whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because of what indicates it, i.e. then who will provide for you other than Him? Al-Zamakhsharī implied a condition after His saying «أمَّن هذا الذي هو جندٌ لكم», its implied form being: if He sends His punishment upon you. There is no need for it from the standpoint of grammatical craft.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {مُكِبّاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of «يَمْشي». And «أَكَبَّ» is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of كَبَّه; one says: كَبَبتُه فَأَكَبَّ ("I threw him on his face and he fell on his face"). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is one of the rarities and anomalies; like it is: قَشَعَتِ الريحُ السَّحابَ فأَقْشَع ('the wind dispersed the clouds and they dispersed'). [Otherwise] nothing of the afʿala pattern is reflexive, and only the bearers of Sībawayh's Book master the like of this. Rather أكَبَّ belongs to the pattern of أَنْفَضَ and أَلامَ, and its meaning is: he entered into the state of falling on the face and became one having it. Likewise أقْشَعَ السحابُ: it entered into dispersal. The reflexive of كَبَّ and قَشَعَ is انكبَّ and انْقَشَعَ."
The Shaykh said: "«مُكِبّاً» is a ḥāl, from «أكبَّ», which is intransitive, while كَبَّ is transitive; He the Exalted said: {فَكُبَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النار} [al-Naml: 90]. The hamza is for entering into a thing, or for becoming; and the reflexive of كَبَّ is انْكَبَّ — you say: كَبَبْتُه فانكَبَّ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: 'and nothing of the afʿala pattern …' up to his saying '… Sībawayh's Book'." End of quote. "This man often boasts of Sībawayh's Book, and how many a text in Sībawayh's Book his sight and his insight were blind to — so much so that the imam Abū al-Ḥajjāj Yūsuf ibn Maʿzūz composed a book in which he mentions where al-Zamakhsharī erred and what he was ignorant of in Sībawayh's Book." End of what the Shaykh said.
Look at this man: how he took al-Zamakhsharī's words, which I have previously quoted from him, embroidered his own wording with them letter by letter, and then set about attacking him with ill manners — as a reward for having been taught those splendid words, which made him say that the reflexive of كَبَّ is انْكَبَّ, not أكَبَّ, and that the hamza in أكَبَّ is for becoming or for entering into a thing! By Allah, had he remained all his life untaught them, he would never have said them. Then he set about reporting, from a man who stands to Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] as the faint star al-Suhā to the moon, that he faulted him on texts of Sībawayh's Book — Allah knows best how sound they are. [The poet said:]
4289 - وكم مِنْ عائبٍ قولاً صحيحاً ... وآفَتُهُ من الفَهْمِ السَّقيمِ
(How many a one faults a sound statement, when the defect lies in his sick understanding.)
And granting [that the faulting is sound], the excellent man is he whose slips can be counted.
His saying: {أَمَّن يَمْشِي}: it is the counterpart (al-muʿādil) of {أَفَمَن يَمْشِي مُكِبّاً}. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«أَهْدَى» is the khabar (predicate) of «مَنْ يمشي», and the khabar of the second «مَنْ» is omitted" — meaning that the original is: "or is the one who walks upright better guided?". There is no need for that, because in the saying «أزيدٌ قائمٌ أم عمروٌ» ("Is Zayd standing, or ʿAmr?") there is no need, from the standpoint of grammatical craft, to omit the khabar; rather you say: it is conjoined to «زيد» as single words are conjoined, and He made the khabar singular because «أم» is for one of two things.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {قَلِيلاً}: the adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of the maṣdar, as is the opinion of Sībawayh; and «ما» is redundant (mazīda), i.e. you give thanks little. The clause beginning «تَشْكرون» is either resumptive, which is the apparent one, or an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because at the time of the making they were not thankful. What is meant by the littleness is non-existence, or its literal sense.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {رَأَوْهُ}: i.e. the thing promised, or the punishment, «زُلْفَةً», i.e. near. So it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. ذا زُلْفَةٍ ("possessing nearness"), or it was made nearness itself for intensiveness. It was also said: «زُلْفَةً» — its implied form being "a place possessing nearness", so it is accusative in the manner of the maṣdar.
His saying: {سِيئَتْ}: the original is ساء, i.e. the punishment and seeing it grieved their faces; then it was made passive. And «ساء» here is not the one synonymous with «بِئْسَ», as you have learnt in what has preceded more than once [Translator's note: the text has «فميا», evidently for «فيما»]. Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī gave the kasra of the sīn a tinge of ḍamma (ishmām), as they did in {سياء بِهِمْ} [Hūd: 77] in Hūd, which has preceded; the rest read it with pure kasra. The verification of this and its morphology, and that there are dialectal forms in it, has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara at His saying {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 11].
His saying: {تَدَّعُونَ}: the majority read it with the dāl doubled and with fatḥa. It was said: from الدَّعْوى (claim), i.e. you claim that there is no Garden and no Fire — al-Ḥasan said this. It was also said: from الدعاء (calling), i.e. you were asking for it and seeking to hasten it. Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Yaʿqūb, Abū Zayd, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Nāfiʿ in the transmission of al-Aṣmaʿī read it with a quiescent dāl, and this supports the view that in the reading of the majority it is from الدعاء.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {آمَنَّا بِهِ وَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا}: it has preceded why the complement of belief was placed after and the complement of reliance placed before, and that placing first conveys restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ). Al-Kisāʾī read «فسيَعْلمون» with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], in view of His saying «الكافرين»; the rest read it in the second person: either as a threat, or as a shift (iltifāt) from the third person intended in al-Kisāʾī's reading.

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying: {غَوْراً}: the khabar (predicate) of «أصبح». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «أصبح» being complete (tāmma), but he considered it far-fetched. He related that it was read «غُؤْوْراً», with a ḍamma on the ghayn and a hamza with ḍamma, then a quiescent wāw, on the fuʿūl pattern, and he made the hamza changed from a wāw with ḍamma [Translator's note: the text has «منقبلة», evidently for «منقلبة», "changed"].

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاعْتَرَفُوا بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسُحْقًا لِأَصْحَابِ السَّعِيرِ (١١))
His saying (فَسُحْقًا): [the implied form is] "so He has imposed on them سُحْقًا (remoteness)", or "so He has made them remote (أَسْحَقَهُمْ) with a remoteness".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ (١٤))
His saying (مَنْ خَلَقَ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the nominative, as the fāʿil (agent) of يَعْلَمُ, and the object is omitted, i.e. "does the Creator not know His creation?"
It is also said: the agent is implied (muḍmar) and «مَنْ» is the object.

ukberi-tibyan:15-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ ذَلُولًا فَامْشُوا فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُوا مِنْ رِزْقِهِ وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ (١٥) أَأَمِنْتُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ أَنْ يَخْسِفَ بِكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَمُورُ (١٦) أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ أَنْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ كَيْفَ نَذِيرِ (١٧))
His saying (النُّشُورُ أَأَمِنْتُمْ) is read with the hamza fully pronounced, according to the original, and with it changed into a wāw in continuous recitation, because of the ḍamma on the rāʾ before it. And (أَنْ يَخْسِفَ) and (أَنْ يُرْسِلَ) are both badals (substitutes) of the badal al-ishtimāl (badal of inclusion) type.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطَّيْرِ فَوْقَهُمْ صَافَّاتٍ وَيَقْبِضْنَ مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا الرَّحْمَنُ إِنَّهُ بِكُلِ شَيْءٍ بَصِيرٌ (١٩))
His saying (فَوْقَهُمْ صَافَّاتٍ): «صَافَّاتٍ» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) with «فَوْقَهُمْ» as an adverb (ẓarf) for it; or «فَوْقَهُمْ» may be a ḥāl and «صَافَّاتٍ» a ḥāl from the pronoun in «فَوْقَهُمْ».
(وَيَقْبِضْنَ) is conjoined to the active participle, construed according to the meaning, i.e. "they spread [their wings] and they close", i.e. "spreading and closing". And (مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا الرَّحْمَنُ) may be resumptive, and may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in يَقْبِضْنَ. The object of يَقْبِضْنَ is omitted, i.e. "their wings".

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمَّنْ هَذَا الَّذِي هُوَ جُنْدٌ لَكُمْ يَنْصُرُكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ الرَّحْمَنِ. . . (٢٠))
His saying (أَمَّنْ): «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and هَذَا is its khabar (predicate); «الَّذِي» with its ṣila (relative clause) is a naʿt (adjective) of هَذَا, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). And (يَنْصُرُكُمْ) is a naʿt of «جُنْدٌ», construed according to its wording; had it been made plural according to the meaning, that would have been permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَمَنْ يَمْشِي مُكِبًّا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ أَهْدَى أَمَّنْ يَمْشِي سَوِيًّا عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٢٢))
His saying (مُكِبًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «عَلَى وَجْهِهِ» is a tawkīd (emphasis); أَهْدَى is the khabar (predicate) of «مَنْ», and the khabar of the second «مَنْ» is omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:3-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا مَا تَرَى فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَنِ مِنْ تَفَاوُتٍ فَارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ هَلْ تَرَى مِنْ فُطُورٍ (٣) ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ يَنْقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ الْبَصَرُ خَاسِئًا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ (٤))
His saying (طِبَاقًا): its singular is طَبَقَةٌ; it is also said: طَبَقٌ.
And (تَفَاوُتٌ), with alif and ḍamma on the wāw, is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of تَفَاوَتَ; and تَفَوُّتٌ, with doubling, is the maṣdar of تَفَوَّتَ; they are two dialectal forms. And (كَرَّتَيْنِ) is a maṣdar, i.e. "two returnings".

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَاؤُكُمْ غَوْرًا فَمَنْ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِمَاءٍ مَعِينٍ (٣٠))
His saying (غَوْرًا): it is the khabar (predicate) of أَصْبَحَ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) if you make it the complete [intransitive] أَصْبَحَ; but this is far-fetched.
And الْغَوْرُ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of الْغَائِر (sinking). It is also read «غُؤُورًا», with ḍamma and hamza, on the pattern فُعُول; the wāw was changed into a hamza because it carried a necessary ḍamma and a wāw came after it. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ (٦))
His saying (كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذَابُ): in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being لِلَّذِينَ.
It is also read in the accusative [عَذَابَ], conjoined to «عَذَابَ السَّعِيرِ».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Mulk (The Dominion)
Makkan
﷽
It has come in the exegesis that it is called ”اَلْمُنْجِيَةَ“ (the Rescuer): it rescues the one who recites it from the punishment of the grave. And it has come in the exegesis that in the Torah (there is): "Sūrat al-Mulk — whoever recites it in a night has done much."

His saying: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ المُلْكُ﴾ means: He is exalted and magnified.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ المَوْتَ والحَياةَ لِيَبْلُوَكم أيُّكم أحْسَنُ عَمَلا﴾ — what ”أيُّكم“ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) is implied; the meaning is: "that He may test you, and so know which of you is best in deed" — a knowledge of what has (actually) occurred. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, already knew what would come from them, but the recompense becomes due through the actual occurrence of the deed from them. ”أيُّ“ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it does not govern it, because it retains its original interrogative sense. This is like His saying: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحْصى لِما لَبِثُوا أمَدًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 12]. According to the grammarians this is to be construed as naming (al-tasmiya) [Translator's note: so printed; the expected term is al-taswiya, "equivalence", i.e. the interrogative of alternatives]: its meaning is the meaning of the (interrogative) alif with ”أمْ“. When you say "قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أيُّكم أفْضَلُ" (I know which of you is better), the meaning is "I know whether Zayd is better or ʿAmr"; ”عَلِمْتُ“ does not govern what comes after the alif, and likewise it does not govern ”أيُّ“; the meaning is the same. The meaning of ﴿خَلَقَ المَوْتَ والحَياةَ﴾ is: He created life for you to test you in it, and created death to raise you and requite you for your deeds. It has come in the exegesis of al-Kalbī: He created death in the form of a black-and-white ram; it passes by nothing but that it dies, treads on nothing but that it dies, and nothing finds its scent but that it dies. And He created life in the form of a piebald mare, larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule; it passes by nothing but that it brings it to life, treads on nothing but that it brings it to life, and nothing finds its scent but that it comes to life. And Allah knows best the reality of that.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقًا ما تَرى في خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَنِ مِن تَفاوُتٍ﴾ — it is also read ”فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَنِ مِن تَفَوُّتٍ“, without alif. In ﴿تَفاوُتٍ﴾ ”تَفاؤُتٍ“ is also permissible, with hamza, the hamza substituting for the wāw with ḍamma. One says ”تَفاوَتَ الشَّيْءُ تَفاوُتًا“ and ”تَفَوَّتَ تَفَوُّتًا“ when a thing is inconsistent. So the meaning is: "You see in His creation of the heaven no inconsistency and no disorder." The meaning of ”طِباقًا“ is: layered one upon another; ”طِباقٌ“ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ”طُوبِقَتْ طِباقًا“.

His saying: ﴿فارْجِعِ البَصَرَ هَلْ تَرى مِن فُطُورٍ﴾ means: do you see in it any gaps or cracks?

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ البَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ يَنْقَلِبْ إلَيْكَ البَصَرُ خاسِئًا وهو حَسِيرٌ﴾ — ”خاسِئًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its meaning is "humbled." ”وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ“: it has grown weary before it could see any flaw in the heaven.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا﴾ means: the one, of the seven heavens, that is near (tadnū) to you.

His saying: ﴿بِمَصابِيحَ﴾ means the stars.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ وبِئْسَ المَصِيرُ﴾ — ”عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ“ is (read) with the accusative and the nominative. The accusative is by conjunction with His saying: "وَأعْتَدْنا لَهم عَذابَ السَّعِيرِ ولِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذابَ جَهَنَّمَ", i.e. "and We have prepared for those who disbelieve in their Lord the punishment of Hell."

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إذا أُلْقُوا فِيها سَمِعُوا لَها شَهِيقًا﴾ — and that (shahīq) is the ugliest of sounds; it is like the braying of a donkey.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿تَكادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ الغَيْظِ﴾ means: it almost bursts apart from its rage against them.

His saying: ﴿كُلَّما أُلْقِيَ فِيها فَوْجٌ سَألَهم خَزَنَتُها ألَمْ يَأْتِكم نَذِيرٌ﴾ ﴿قالُوا بَلى قَدْ جاءَنا نَذِيرٌ﴾ [al-Mulk: 9] — this rebuke is an increase for them in the punishment. Then they confessed their ignorance and said: ﴿لَوْ كُنّا نَسْمَعُ أوْ نَعْقِلُ ما كُنّا في أصْحابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾ [al-Mulk: 10], i.e. had we listened as one listens who takes in and reflects, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze; or had we reasoned as one reasons who discerns and considers, we would not be among the people of the Fire.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿فاعْتَرَفُوا بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسُحْقًا﴾ — it is also transmitted as ”فَسُحُقًا“ with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ. ”سُحْقًا“ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is "may Allah remove them far away (asḥaqahum) with a removal," i.e. may Allah distance them from His mercy. ”اَلسَّحِيقُ“ is the distant.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿فامْشُوا في مَناكِبِها﴾ means: on its mountains; and it is said: on its sides; and it is said: on its roads. The most likely interpretation — and Allah knows best — is that of those who said "on its mountains," because His saying ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأرْضَ ذَلُولا﴾ means "He made travelling on it easy for you"; and if travelling on its mountains is possible for you, that is the utmost in making it subservient.

His saying: ﴿وَإلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ﴾ means: Allah, who created the heavens without pillars and without inconsistency in them, and created the earth and made it subservient to you, is able to resurrect (yunshira) you, i.e. to raise you.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا هي تَمُورُ﴾ — the meaning of ”تَمُورُ“ is: it revolves (heaves).

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿أنْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكم حاصِبًا﴾ means: just as He sent upon the people of Lūṭ the stones that pelted them.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى الطَّيْرِ فَوْقَهم صافّاتٍ ويَقْبِضْنَ﴾ — He made clear to them, by the creation of the heavens and the earths, what points them to His oneness; and He made (it) clear to them by subjecting the birds in the air of the sky, spreading their wings and folding them: ﴿ما يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إلا الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ — by His power.

zajjaj:22-22.t: ﴿أفَمَن يَمْشِي مُكِبًّا عَلى وجْهِهِ أهْدى أمَّنْ يَمْشِي سَوِيًّا عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the believer is following the straight path, and that the disbeliever in his error is like one who walks prone upon his face. It has come in the exegesis that the disbeliever will walk on his face in the Hereafter: «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "How will they walk on their faces?" He said: "The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces."»

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأوْهُ زُلْفَةً سِيئَتْ وُجُوهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ — it was also read ”سُيْئَتْ“, giving the sīn a tinge (ishmām) of ḍamma; and ”سِيَتْ“ is permissible, dropping the hamza and casting its vowel onto the yāʾ. The meaning is: "When they saw the punishment near (zulfa), i.e. close, the faces of those who disbelieved were grieved: evil became apparent in them." ﴿وَقِيلَ هَذا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَدَّعُونَ﴾ — it was also read ”تَدْعُونَ“, from ”دَعَوْتُ، أدْعُو“. As for ”تَدَّعُونَ“, it has come in the exegesis: "you deny." Its interpretation in the language is: "This is that on account of which you used to make false and lying claims," i.e. you used to claim that when you died and became dust and bones you would not be brought forth. Whoever read ”تَدْعُونَ“, undoubled, the meaning is: "This is what you used to seek to hasten, calling on Allah in your saying: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ أوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]." It is also possible that the meaning of ”تَدَّعُونَ“ is this as well: ”تَفْتَعِلُونَ“ from ”اَلدُّعاءُ“ (calling), and (alternatively) ”تَفْتَعِلُونَ“ from ”اَلدَّعْوى“ (claiming); that is possible — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ أصْبَحَ ماؤُكم غَوْرًا﴾ means: sunk (ghāʾir). It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with which a noun is described, so you say ”ماءٌ غَوْرٌ“, ”ماءانِ غَوْرٌ“ and ”مِياهٌ غَوْرٌ“, just as you say ”هَذا عَدْلٌ“, ”هَذانِ عَدْلٌ“ and ”هَؤُلاءِ عَدْلٌ“. The meaning of ”مَعِينٌ“ is: flowing from springs; and it has come in the exegesis: on the surface, the meaning being that it appears from the springs.
